sentences.text: Rhomaleosaurus is an extinct genus of rhomaleosaurid pliosauroid known from Northamptonshire and Yorkshire in the United Kingdom.
Its unique skull adaptation would have enabled Rhomaleosaurus to hunt its prey in a manner similar to some modern shark species.
The animal may have been capable of detecting scents while submerged by forcing water through passages in its skull containing sensory organs.
The holotype fossil was unearthed in July 1848 at an alum quarry near Whitby, Yorkshire, England.
The fossil was introduced to Sir Philip Crampton in 1853 by the Marquess of Normanby.
Harry Govier Seeley erected the new genus Rhomaleosaurus in 1874 based on this finding.
The skull of the holotype was not finally prepared and described until 2006, allowing for a re-study of the genus.
Rhomaleosaurus coexisted with the ichthyosaur Temnodontosaurus, and both acted as top-tier consumers feeding on ammonites, plesiosaurs, and ichthyosaurs.
This adaptation would have enabled Rhomaleosaurus to hunt its prey in a manner similar to some modern shark species.
Rhomaleosaurus may have been capable of detecting scents while submerged by forcing water through passages in its skull containing sensory organs.
The parent group of Rhomaleosaurus is Rhomaleosauridae.
According to Smith (2007), the genus Rhomaleosaurus comprises only three valid species: R. cramptoni, R. thorntoni, and R. zetlandicus.
Smith (2007) and Smith and Dyke (2008) determined that R. megacephalus belongs to Eurycleidus and R. victor represents a new genus named Meyerasaurus.
Today, the taxon Thaumatosaurus is considered a nomen dubium because its holotype can at most be classified as an indeterminate Pliosauroidea.
Specimens previously considered as Thaumatosaurus now represent the holotypes of Eurycleidus, Meyerasaurus, and Rhomaleosaurus.
The time range for Rhomaleosaurus is from the Hettangian to the Toarcian, between 201.4 and 174.7 million years ago.
